learning: Compare max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and progress per track with iteration 1. If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.25, the lighter mass or the higher kp is the likely cause: reduce kp toward 6.0 first. If max_error stays above 0.06 m with line loss still present, the next lever is geometry (sensor row or sensor_size), not gain.
notes: Complete robot for the Builder's wheel_track 0.14 m, mass 0.5 kg geometry with the seven-sensor array unchanged. kp is raised to 7.0 to offset the lower yaw rate per unit of turn on the wider track.
rationale: Iteration 1 (seven sensors, kp 6.0) did not reduce max_error: it stayed at 0.062 to 0.068 m on every track, above the 0.06 m off-track floor, and line_loss_events stayed at about 1 per run. Sensing span is therefore not the limiting factor, and the robot leaves the tape while the sensors still see it. The Builder's geometry for this iteration widens wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.14 m and lowers mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg, with the sensor array unchanged. The Integrator must compensate for the wider track. Per the contract, turn rate = (right wheel speed - left wheel speed) / wheel_track, so for the same PWM difference from turn, the wider track gives about 0.12/0.14 = 0.86 of the yaw rate. To keep the steering response per metre of offset the same as iteration 1, I scale kp by 0.14/0.12 = 1.17, from 6.0 to 7.0. The signal weights stay at [-2, -1.33, -0.67, 0, 0.67, 1.33, 2] because the sensor positions are unchanged. ki (0.2) and kd (0.3) stay as they were, since steering oscillation in iteration 1 was low (0.11 to 0.23). The lighter 0.5 kg mass lowers yaw inertia, so the same kp should respond somewhat faster, which is a risk for oscillation. base_speed stays at 1.8 and line_loss stays at last_direction, which kept the robot turning toward the tape after a loss in earlier races. Expected result: max_error below 0.06 m on s-bend and slalom, and line_loss_events closer to zero. The result will be read against iteration 1 per track.
